html:
A steel arch bridge over the gorge of the Zambezi just below Victoria Falls, opened in 1905. It carries a railway, a road and a footpath, and now links Zimbabwe and Zambia.

It was part of Cecil Rhodes's dream of a Cape to Cairo railway through British territory. Rhodes is said to have wanted the bridge close enough for passengers to feel the spray of the falls. He died in 1902 and never saw it. The engineer George Hobson designed it, and the parts were made in England and assembled from both sides of the gorge.

The bridge let the railway of the British South Africa Company run north into Northern Rhodesia, reaching the mines at Broken Hill by 1906 and later serving the Copperbelt. The Cape to Cairo line was never finished. Today the bridge is a border crossing and a place for bungee jumping.
